''[[Ariel (TV series)|Ariel]]'') }} | significant_other = [[List of The Little Mermaid characters#Prince Eric|Prince Eric]] (ex-fiancé; as Vanessa) | children = Uma (daughter; ''[[Descendants (franchise)|Descendants]]'') | relatives = [[List of The Little Mermaid characters#Attina, Alana, Adella, Aquata, Arista and Andrina|Attina, Alana, Adella, Aquata, Arista, Andrina]], and [[Ariel (The Little Mermaid)|Ariel]] (nieces in some media){{cite magazine|date=April 4, 2023|url=https://ew.com/movies/the-little-mermaid-halle-bailey-melissa-mccarthy-cover-story/|title=A deep dive into the live-action 'Little Mermaid' Romano|last=Romano|first=Nick|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]}} | nationality = Atlantican | lbl22 = Pet(s) | data22 = [[List of The Little Mermaid characters#Flotsam and Jetsam|Flotsam and Jetsam]] }} '''Ursula''' is a fictional character who appears in [[Walt Disney Pictures]]' animated film ''[[The Little Mermaid (1989 film)|The Little Mermaid]]'' (1989). Voiced by actress [[Pat Carroll]], Ursula is a villainous [[Cecaelia]]n [[Witchcraft|sea witch]] who offers [[mermaid]] princess [[Ariel (The Little Mermaid)|Ariel]] a temporary opportunity to become human so that she may earn the love of [[List of Disney's The Little Mermaid characters#Prince Eric|Prince Eric]] within three days. However, Ursula is determined to sabotage Ariel's chances in order to usurp [[King Triton (The Little Mermaid)|King Triton]]'s position as ruler of the oceans. Created by directors and screenwriters [[Ron Clements]] and [[John Musker]], Ursula is based on the sea witch character who appears in the 1837 fairy tale "[[The Little Mermaid]]" by [[Hans Christian Andersen]]. However, unlike the minor role of the character in the fairy tale, Ursula's role was greatly expanded into a much more prominent villain for the film. Disney had struggled to cast Ursula for a year, during which the role was well sought after by several coveted television actresses at the time. Clements and Musker disagreed with lyricist [[Howard Ashman]] about who should voice the character. While the directors had written the role with [[Bea Arthur]] in mind, Ashman intended to offer it to [[soap opera]] star [[Joan Collins]]; both actresses rejected the part. When Ashman cast his second choice, Broadway actress [[Elaine Stritch]], as Ursula, both stage veterans disagreed about the manner in which Ursula's song "[[Poor Unfortunate Souls]]" would be performed, and [[Pat Carroll]] was finally hired to replace Stritch after Ashman fired her. Deepening her own voice for the role, Carroll based her performance on a combination of [[William Shakespeare|Shakespearean]] actresses and [[Car salesman|car salespeople]]. Animated by [[Ruben A. Aquino]], Ursula's original design was inspired by several different [[Marine biology|sea creatures]], including [[manta ray]]s and [[Scorpaeniformes|scorpion fish]], before Clements finally decided to base the character on an [[octopus]]; her number of [[tentacles]] was reduced from eight to six for financial reasons. Ursula's appearance was also inspired by American actor and drag queen [[Divine (performer)|Divine]]. When ''The Little Mermaid'' was first released in 1989, Ursula was immediately embraced as one of Disney's best villains, and continues to be ranked highly among the studio's greatest by the media. Praised for being humorous and frightening, the character has garnered positive reviews from film critics, some of whom dubbed her Disney's strongest villain in decades. Meanwhile, Carroll's performance has continued to garner acclaim to the point that the role has eclipsed her previous body of work, ultimately becoming virtually synonymous with the character. ==Development== ===Conception and writing=== At the behest of Disney executives [[Michael Eisner]] and [[Jeffrey Katzenberg]], director and screenwriter [[Ron Clements]] was among several film-makers instructed to research new story ideas that could potentially be adapted into the studio's next major animated film release.{{cite web|url=http://www.beliefnet.com/columnists/moviemom/2013/09/interview-ron-clements-john-musker-little-mermaid-disney.html|title=Interview: Ron Clements and John Musker of "The Little Mermaid"|last=Minow|first=Nell|website=Beliefnet|publisher=Beliefnet, Inc|access-date=April 1, 2016|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192125/http://www.beliefnet.com/columnists/moviemom/2013/09/interview-ron-clements-john-musker-little-mermaid-disney.html|url-status=dead}} Clements first discovered [[Hans Christian Andersen]]'s classic fairy tale "[[The Little Mermaid]]" at a local bookstore, and began deliberating why Disney had never attempted to adapt the story before. Clements eventually learned that [[Walt Disney]] himself had actually attempted to adapt the fairy tale into a feature-length animated film as early as the 1930s,{{cite web|url=http://www.moviefone.com/2014/11/14/the-little-mermaid-facts/|title='The Little Mermaid' Facts: 25 Things You Didn't Know About the Disney Masterpiece|last=Susman|first=Gary|date=November 14, 2014|website=Moviefone|publisher=Aol Inc|access-date=April 1, 2016}} but the project was ultimately shelved due in part to its sad ending.{{cite web|url=http://metro.co.uk/2015/03/15/10-things-you-probably-didnt-know-about-the-little-mermaid-5104832/|title=10 things you probably didn't know about The Little Mermaid|last=Duncan|first=Amy|date=March 15, 2010|website=Metro|access-date=April 1, 2016}} Clements suggested "The Little Mermaid" to Katzenberg, who finally [[Greenlight|greenlit]] it after having first rejected it. Hardly present in Andersen's original story,{{cite web|url=http://emgn.com/entertainment/15-exciting-facts-about-the-little-mermaid-you-never-knew/|title=15 Exciting Facts About The Little Mermaid You Never Knew!|website=EMGN|access-date=April 1, 2016}} the [[Witchcraft|sea witch]] is not a prominent character and lacks a [[proper name]].{{cite web|url=https://ohmy.disney.com/movies/2014/08/16/15-things-you-didnt-know-about-the-little-mermaid/|title=15 THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE LITTLE MERMAID|last=Brandon|first=Emily|date=2014|website=Oh My Disney|publisher=Disney|access-date=April 1, 2016}} Among Clements' ideas to alter the story, the film-maker decided to "make the witch more of a villain", describing Ursula as "a fun character to develop" into such. In Andersen's tale, the sea witch is not a villainess as much as she is "a disreputable mermaid."{{Cite web|url=http://www.disneyvillains.net/Ursula.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080120051646/http://www.disneyvillains.net/Ursula.php|url-status=usurped|archive-date=January 20, 2008|title=Ursula – The Little Mermaid (1989)|website=Disney Villains|access-date=April 20, 2016}} JR Thorpe of ''[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]'' agreed that, in Andersen's story, "The sea witch isn't the enemy". Instead, "[[Human nature|human ... nature]] is."{{Cite web|url=http://www.bustle.com/articles/65813-9-ways-the-original-little-mermaid-by-hans-christian-andersen-is-actually-seriously-disturbing|title=9 Ways The Original 'Little Mermaid' By Hans Christian Andersen Is Actually Seriously Disturbing|last=Thorpe|first=JR|date=February 25, 2015|website=Bustle|access-date=April 22, 2016}} While the original sea witch is willing to help the little mermaid despite the fact that she openly disagrees with her motives, Ursula is only interested in helping Ariel in the hopes of ultimately overthrowing her father. Emma James of ''[[Teen Ink]]'' observed that in addition to giving the character the name "Ursula", the studio "changed her role as a catalyst in the tale, and morphed her actions into those of an antagonist."{{Cite web|url=http://www.teenink.com/nonfiction/academic/article/586214/The-Evolution-of-the-Little-Mermaid/|title=The Evolution of the Little Mermaid|last=James|first=Emma|website=Teen Ink|publisher=Emerson Media|access-date=April 25, 2016}} Unlike the sea witch, Ursula deliberately intervenes in an attempt to keep the mermaid from success.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vjdQBwAAQBAJ&q=ursula+matriarchy+disney&pg=PA69|title=Emerson Goes to the Movies: Individualism in Walt Disney Company's Post-1989 Animated Films|last=Fruzińska|first=Justyna|publisher=Cambridge Scholars Publishing|year=2014|isbn=9781443869157|location=United Kingdom|pages=69}} Lyricist, producer and writer [[Howard Ashman]] had originally envisioned Ursula's relationship with [[King Triton (The Little Mermaid)|King Triton]] as a [[soap opera]], and thus drew inspiration from soap opera actress [[Joan Collins]].{{Cite web|url=http://mentalfloss.com/article/67862/10-disney-characters-who-were-almost-voiced-lister|title=10 Disney Characters Who Were Almost Voiced By an A-Lister|last=Malach|first=Maggie|date=August 28, 2015|website=Mental Floss|publisher=Mental Floss, Inc|access-date=April 2, 2016}} Ursula was originally conceived as Triton's sister,{{Cite web|url=https://ca.movies.yahoo.com/blogs/wide-screen/5-disney-villains-who-deserve-their-own-movies-181045442.html|title=5 Disney Villains Who Deserve Their Own Movies|last=Perkins|first=Will|date=May 27, 2014|website=Yahoo! Movies|access-date=April 28, 2016}} which would have naturally made the character Ariel's aunt,{{cite web|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/inarelationshipwithpizza/17things-you-probably-didnt-know-about-the-littl-7shb|title=17 Things You Probably Didn't Know About Disney's "The Little Mermaid"|date=December 4, 2012|website=BuzzFeed|publisher=BuzzFeed, Inc|access-date=April 1, 2016}} but the idea was ultimately abandoned.{{cite web|url=http://www.j-14.com/posts/10-totally-mind-blowing-facts-about-the-little-mermaid-17164/photos/the-little-mermaid-9-9728#photo-anchor|title=10 Totally Mind-Blowing Facts About 'The Little Mermaid'|last=Van de Wall|first=Virginia|date=October 1, 2013|website=J-14|access-date=April 1, 2016}} However, their [[blood relationship]] is still vaguely alluded to when the character mentions a time during which she actually lived in Triton's palace.{{cite web|url=http://mentalfloss.com/article/59003/11-things-you-might-not-know-about-little-mermaid|title=11 Things You Might Not Know About 'The Little Mermaid'|last=Oneill|first=Therese|date=October 28, 2015|website=Mental Floss|publisher=Mental Floss, Inc|access-date=April 1, 2016}} Clements and Musker had originally intended for Ursula to remain her original size at the end of the film.{{cite web|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/top/2529/8/The-Little-Mermaid-1989-50-things-you-might-not-know-about-your-favorite-Disney-films-1989-1997.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140622032739/http://www.deseretnews.com/top/2529/8/The-Little-Mermaid-1989-50-things-you-might-not-know-about-your-favorite-Disney-films-1989-1997.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 22, 2014|title=50 things you might not know about your favorite Disney films, 1989-1997 edition|last=Hicken|first=Jackie|date=June 17, 2014|website=Desert News|access-date=April 1, 2016}} However, Katzenberg had just recently seen the film ''[[Die Hard]]'' (1988), which inspired him to request a "bigger" ending for ''The Little Mermaid'', and thus he instructed the writers to have Ursula grow much larger in size during her [[Climax (narrative)|climactic]] fight with Ariel and Eric. ===Voice and music=== [[Pat Carroll]] was the voice actress of Ursula from 1989 to her death in 2022, with her final role as Ursula being posthumous in ''[[Disney Dreamlight Valley]]''.{{cite web| url=https://deadline.com/2022/07/pat-carroll-dead-voice-of-ursula-in-the-little-mermaid-was-95-1235081904/| title=Pat Carroll Dies: Veteran Actress Of Stage, TV, Film And Voice Of Ursula In 'The Little Mermaid' Was 95| first=Bruce| last=Haring| work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]| date=July 31, 2022| accessdate=July 31, 2022}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.wic.org/bio/pcarroll.htm|title=Pat Carroll|website=Women's International Center|access-date=April 2, 2016}}{{cite web |title=Sea Witch Voices (Little Mermaid) |url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/characters/The-Little-Mermaid/Sea-Witch/ |access-date=April 14, 2025 |publisher=Behind The Voice Actors}} A green check mark indicates that a role has been confirmed using a screenshot (or collage of screenshots) of a title's list of voice actors and their respective characters found in its credits or other reliable sources of information. Carroll was not the filmmakers' first choice for the role; Clements, Musker and Ashman had long debated who should voice the villainess,{{cite web|url=http://jimhillmedia.com/editor_in_chief1/b/jim_hill/archive/2007/06/15/why-for-pat-carroll-wasn-t-actually-disney-s-first-choice-to-voice-ursula-in-the-little-mermaid.aspx|title=Why (For) Pat Carroll wasn't actually Disney's first choice to voice Ursula in "The Little Mermaid"|last=Hill|first=Jim|date=June 14, 2007|website=Jim Hill Media|access-date=March 4, 2016}} the casting of whom was long and tedious, spanning an entire year.{{Cite web|url=http://howardashman.com/blog/john-musker-question-countdown-number-7/|title=John Musker Question Countdown – Number 7|website=Howard Ashman|date=26 March 2012 |publisher=Shoptalk Ltd|access-date=April 2, 2016}}{{cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/jim-hill/which-1980s-tv-favorites_b_6465252.html|title=Which 1980s TV 1, 2016}} In his book ''Makin' Toons: Inside the Most Popular Animated TV Shows and Movies'', author Allan Neuwirth documented that the filmmakers searched "for just the right performer who could put across the deep-voiced, world-weary, [[deadpan]] villainess they had in mind–but never quite snaring their catch".{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xEctAgAAQBAJ&q=pat+carroll+ursula+the+little+mermaid&pg=PT253|title=Makin' Toons: Inside the Most Popular Animated TV Shows and Movies|last=Neuwirth|first=Allan|publisher=Skyhorse Publishing, Inc|year=2013|isbn=9781621531975|location=United States|via=Google Books}} While Ashman was interested in actress [[Joan Collins]] because he was a fan of her performance as [[Alexis Colby]] in the [[soap opera]] ''[[Dynasty (1981 TV series)|Dynasty]]'', Clements and Musker favored actress [[Bea Arthur]], for whom they had actually written the role, describing Ursula as "having a Bea Arthur-type [[Bass (voice type)|basso]] voice" in early drafts of their screenplay. Clements and Musker fully expected Arthur to accept the role because she had already been working for Disney's [[Touchstone Television]] on the sitcom ''[[The Golden Girls]]''. However, Arthur's agent resented the directors-writers for insinuating that her client voice a witch, refusing to even present the script to the actress. With Arthur eliminated, Clements and Musker were forced to [[audition]] several other popular television actresses of the decade, including [[Nancy Marchand]], [[Charlotte Rae]] and [[Roseanne Barr]], the last of whom had originally auditioned for the supporting role of chambermaid Carlotta. Amused by her [[nasal voice]], Howard invited the comedian to read for Ursula, but concluded that her approach was ultimately not suitable for the character. Jazz singer [[Nancy Wilson (jazz singer)|Nancy Wilson]] also auditioned. [[Jennifer Saunders]] auditioned too but was turned down, though her audition tape survived and was somehow found by [[Steven Spielberg]] in 2002, which led him to insist [[Andrew Adamson]], [[Kelly Asbury]] and [[Conrad Vernon]] to cast her as the scheming [[Fairy Godmother (Shrek)|Fairy Godmother]] in ''[[Shrek 2]]'' (2004).{{cite web|url=https://bashful269.wordpress.com/2020/12/04/things-you-never-noticed-in-44-the-little-mermaid/|title=Things You Never Noticed In… #43: The Little Mermaid|last=The Reviewing Network|date=December 4, 2020|website=The Reviewing Network|access-date=May 21, 2025}} Meanwhile, Ashman himself had been similarly unsuccessful in recruiting Collins because ''Dynasty'' producer [[Aaron Spelling]] feared that the actress' reputation would be jeopardized should she voice an animated character. Thus, Ashman pursued [[Musical theatre|Broadway]] veteran [[Elaine Stritch]], of whom he had been a long-time fan. The audition process for Ursula required each hopeful to both recite a scene from the film and perform a Broadway-style song of their choice. The finalists became Clements and Musker's Rae versus Ashman's Stritch, the latter of whom ultimately won the role over Rae with her preferred rendition of Ursula's song "[[Poor Unfortunate Souls]]". Musker described Stritch's approach to Ursula as "an eccentric, loopy reading". However, Stritch and Ashman soon began to experience creative differences over "Poor Unfortunate Souls" because the actress refused to follow the lyricist's "very specific directions". After refusing to perform the song at Ashman's preferred tempo (combined with her [[alcoholism]]), the songwriter fired Stritch from the project, thus forcing Clements and Musker to find a replacement with yet another round of auditions. Carroll first learned of ''The Little Mermaid'' from her agent, and immediately agreed to audition for Ursula because she had always wanted to voice a Disney character. However, the actress felt that her chances were slim to none upon realizing that her competition largely consisted of famous film and television actresses. Musker described Carroll's audition approach as a hybrid of actors [[Maurice Evans (actor)|Maurice Evans]] and [[Tallulah Bankhead]]. Although confident in both her acting and singing auditions, Carroll did not hear back from her agent about the role until a year afterward, by which time she had already forgotten she had ever auditioned. Upon being cast, Carroll was entirely committed to the role, giving it complete precedence over all other jobs and projects at the time. Carroll's first task was to record "Poor Unfortunate Souls", her approach to which was remarkably different than Stritch's, first asking Howard to demonstrate exactly how he would like her to perform the song before attempting it. Carroll completely credits Ashman with her delivery, explaining, "I got the whole attitude from him ... and his shoulders would twitch a certain way, and his eyes would go a certain way ... I got more about that character from Howard singing that song than from anything else." Carroll also borrowed Ursula's habit of saying "innit" instead of "isn't it" from Ashman. Despite their strong working relationship, Carroll described working with Ashman and composer [[Alan Menken]] as a "brutal" experience because of the songwriters' "military" approach; she would often return home from recording sessions with blown vocal cords. After complaining to her about one of her recording sessions, Carroll recalled her daughter, filmmaker [[Tara Karsian]], reassuring her that "you're in something that fifty years from now may be shown ... What you're working on now will be seen by our children, and our grandchildren, and our great-grandchildren". Describing her own performance as [[William Shakespeare|Shakespearean]], Carroll perceived Ursula as an "ex-Shakespearean actress who now sold cars", which inspired her dry, theatrical interpretation. Carroll also deepened her own voice for the role.{{Cite web|url=http://www.fast-rewind.com/making_littlemermaid.htm|title=Making Of...The Little Mermaid Behind The Scenes|website=The 80s Movies Rewind|publisher=Fast-Rewind.com|access-date=April 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107050713/http://www.fast-rewind.com/making_littlemermaid.htm|archive-date=November 7, 2014|url-status=dead}} When Carroll watched the completed film for the first time, she was frightened by her own performance, comparing it to actress [[Margaret Hamilton (actress)|Margaret Hamilton]]'s performance as the [[Wicked Witch of the West]] in the film ''[[The Wizard of Oz (1939 film)|The Wizard of Oz]]'' (1939). Actress [[Jodi Benson]], who voices Ariel, briefly provides the voice of "Vanessa", Ursula's beautiful human [[Alter ego|alter-ego]], in lieu of Carroll.{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/jim-hill/this-little-mermaid-has-l_b_4323101.html|title=This 'Little Mermaid' Has Legs: Disney Legend Jodi Benson Looks Back on 25 Years of Voicing the Character of Ariel|last=Hill|first=Jim|date=November 22, 2013|website=The Huffington Post|publisher=TheHuffingtonPost.com, Inc|access-date=April 2, 2016}} On June 28, 2019, it was announced that [[Melissa McCarthy]] was in talks to play Ursula in the live-action remake of ''[[The Little Mermaid (2023 film)|The Little Mermaid]]'', directed by [[Rob Marshall]].{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/melissa-mccarthy-little-mermaid-ursula-1203217481/|title=Melissa McCarthy in Talks to Play Ursula in Live-Action 'Little Mermaid' (EXCLUSIVE)|first=Justin|last=Kroll|date=June 28, 2019|work=Variety|access-date=July 1, 2019}} On February 18, 2020, McCarthy confirmed her casting as the villainess during an interview on ''[[The Ellen DeGeneres Show]]'': “I play Ursula, the sea witch. It is so fun, we're just in rehearsals. It's been an absolute blast. Stepping into the world of Rob Marshall, it's like a fever dream, I just went to London for a week, I was like, ‘I don't get to go to dance camp for a week.’ All day he's like, ‘Do you want to slide down this 40-foot clamshell?’ I'm like, ‘Yes! Of course, I do. What are you, crazy?’ It's been wildly creative.”{{cite web |url=https://insidethemagic.net/2020/02/melissa-mccarthy-ursula-tm1/|title=Melissa McCarthy Talks Becoming Ursula for Disney's Live-Action "Little Mermaid"|website=Inside the Magic |last=Muscaro|first=TJ|date=February 18, 2020|access-date=May 26, 2020}} In December 2020, McCarthy stated that she would hopefully begin filming the movie in January 2021.{{Cite news|url=https://people.com/movies/melissa-mccarthy-gives-update-on-playing-ursula-in-live-action-little-mermaid-its-just-so-fun/|title=Melissa McCarthy Gives Update on Playing Ursula in Live-Action Little Mermaid: 'It's Just So Fun'|last=Harmata|first=Claudia|date=December 2, 2020|work=People.com|language=en|access-date=December 3, 2020}} McCarthy eventually began filming her scenes in April 2021.{{Cite news|url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/VIDEO-Melissa-McCarthy-Teases-Her-Upcoming-Role-As-Ursula-20210329|title=VIDEO: Melissa McCarthy Teases Her Upcoming Role As Ursula in THE LITTLE MERMAID|last=Tube|first=Stage|date=March 29, 2021|work=Broadwayworld.com|language=en|access-date=March 29, 2021}} Later that year, McCarthy described the experience of playing Ursula as "glorious" and adding, "The world of Disney and (director) Rob Marshall is a world that I wish everyone could experience because it's so creative, kind and lovely. Going to singing class every day ... I got to record with an orchestra, which is a mind-bender for someone who is not a singer ... but it was such a fun process. It's going to be incredible ... To me, Ursula is everything. She's one of my absolute favorite villains so to play her was delicious."{{cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/little-mermaid-movie-ursula-character-melissa-mccarthy-response/|title=Melissa McCarthy Says Playing Ursula in The Little Mermaid is Glorious|first=Abigal|last=Ong-Pizarro|date=September 27, 2021|work=Screen Rant|access-date=July 22, 2022}} [[Jessica Alexander]] played Vanessa, Ursula's beautiful human [[alter ego]]. [she] takes the opportunity to go all-out, unleashing her villainous side in her final scene."{{cite web |last1=Iacobucci |first1=Jordan |title=10 Best Performances in ''The Little Mermaid'' Live-Action Remake |url=https://www.cbr.com/little-mermaid-live-action-remake-best-performances/ |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |access-date=June 7, 2023 |language=en |date=May 27, 2023}} [[Kacey Musgraves]] was also considered for the role.{{cite web|url=https://movieweb.com/kacey-musgraves-little-mermaid-disney/|title=Disney's The Little Mermaid Remake Goes After Grammy Winner Kacey Musgraves|last=Fuge|first=Jonathan|date=July 24, 2020|website=[[MovieWeb]]|access-date=May 27, 2023|archive-date=December 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214000325/https://movieweb.com/kacey-musgraves-little-mermaid-disney/|url-status=live}} ===Design=== {{Annotated image | image = Pink Flamingos trailer screenshot (1).jpg | image-width = 306 | image-left = -50 | image-top = -30 | width = 220 | height = 160 | float = left | annotations = | caption = Ursula's character in ''The Little Mermaid'' was inspired by the [[drag queen]] [[Divine (performer)|Divine]]. }} During production of ''The Little Mermaid'', Ursula's design evolved and transformed dramatically. Animator [[Glen Keane]]'s earliest sketches of Ursula were drawn to resemble Rae, specifically based on the actress' audition for the role. The short-lived casting of Stritch as Ursula and her subsequent performance eventually inspired the animators to design the character as "a tall, thin regal-looking sea witch" based on [[manta ray]]s and [[Scorpaeniformes|scorpion fish]], complete with a long cape. At one point, Ursula had also been drawn with spikes to resemble a [[Spikefish|spinefish]]. Ursula's appearance was largely inspired by American actor and [[drag queen]] [[Divine (actor)|Divine]],{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pdCrF4JxKDIC&q=ursula+feminism+the+little+mermaid&pg=PA182|title=From Mouse to Mermaid: The Politics of Film, Gender, and Culture|last1=Bell|first1=Elizabeth|last2=Haas|first2=Lynda|last3=Sells|first3=Laura|publisher=Indiana University Press|year=1995|isbn=9780253209788|location=United States|pages=182}} who was best known for his frequent appearances in several films directed by filmmaker [[John Waters]]. Similarities were first drawn between the character and the actor after animator [[Rob Minkoff]] sketched "a vampy overweight matron", to which Ashman responded, "She looks like a [[Miami Beach, Florida|Miami Beach]] matron ... playing [[Mahjong|Mah Jong]] by the pool.”{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/article/read-how-divine-inspired-ursula-sea-witch-230938|title=Read This: How Divine inspired Ursula The Sea Witch|last=Dart|first=Chris|date=January 19, 2016|website=A. V. Club|publisher=Onion Inc|access-date=April 1, 2016}} The character shares Divine's signature [[eye makeup]], jewelry and body type while originally sporting a [[Mohawk hairstyle|Mohawk]] and tattoos,{{cite web|url=https://indie-cinema.com/2024/09/interview-with-film-director-and-animation-legend-john-musker/|work=Indie Cinema Magazine|author=Diana Ringo|title=Interview with film director and animation legend John Musker|date=September 8, 2024}} the mohawk was borrowed from the actor's ''Female Trouble'' (1974) character Dawn Davenport. However, Minkoff had been drawing the character with a shark's tail at the time. Clements eventually decided to place Ursula's head on top of the body of an octopus instead, which ultimately resulted in her current design. The animators then studied the way in which octopuses move, explaining, "There was a very kind of seductive and yet scary aspect", which they incorporated into the character's own gait. The ''Female Trouble''-inspired Mohawk and tattooed look was ultimately discarded because Disney felt that it would be "too over-the-top" for the film.{{Cite web|url=http://moviepilot.com/posts/2766413|title=(WATCH) Things you probably didn't know about "The Little Mermaid"|last=Portolan|first=Daniel|date=March 9, 2015|website=Moviepilot|access-date=April 20, 2016|archive-date=May 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160507042334/http://moviepilot.com/posts/2766413|url-status=dead}} Additionally, Ursula's face was also inspired by that of [[Madame Medusa]] from Disney's ''[[The Rescuers]]'' (1977)''.''{{cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/movies/bp/17-things-didn-t-know-little-mermaid-201752088.html|title=17 Things You Didn't Know About 'The Little Mermaid'|last=Min|first=Lilian|date=September 20, 2013|website=Yahoo!|access-date=April 1, 2016|archive-date=April 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160413141856/https://www.yahoo.com/movies/bp/17-things-didn-t-know-little-mermaid-201752088.html|url-status=dead}} According to ''The Gospel according to Disney: Faith, Trust, and Pixie Dust'' author Mark I. Pinsky, Ursula became "the most [[Grotesque body|grotesque]] characterization Disney ... have created for a female villain" at that time.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=N551BwAAQBAJ&q=ursula+norma+desmond&pg=PA140|title=The Gospel according to Disney: Faith, Trust, and Pixie Dust|last=Pinsky|first=Mark I.|publisher=Westminster John Knox Press|year=2004|isbn=9781611644272|location=United Kingdom|pages=140}} Having animated previous Disney villains, Keane was originally approached to be the supervising animator of Ursula, but declined in favor of animating Ariel because he longed to do something different.{{Cite web|url=http://aimeemajor.com/anim/aagleninterview.html|title=Glen Keane Interview August 22, 1990|date=August 22, 1990|website=AimeeMajor.com|access-date=April 25, 2016}} Thus, Keane was replaced by [[Ruben A. Aquino]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.dvdizzy.com/littlemermaid-platinumeditionb.html|title=The Little Mermaid: Platinum Edition DVD Review|date=October 3, 2006|website=DVDizzy.com|access-date=April 23, 2016}} The character was originally drawn with a full set of eight tentacles similar to a real-life octopus, which were eventually reduced to a more manageable six because the original amount would have been too difficult and costly to animate.{{cite web|url=http://thefw.com/things-you-didnt-know-about-disneys-the-little-mermaid/|title=10 Things You Didn't Know About Disney's 'The Little Mermaid'|last=Franks-Allen|first=Sara|website=The FW|date=26 September 2013 |publisher=SCREENCRUSH NETWORK|access-date=April 1, 2016}} According to Carroll,{{Cite web|url=https://deaditeden.com/2015/11/18/happy-26th-birthday-to-the-little-mermaid-here-are-a-few-facts-you-didnt-know/|title=Happy 26th birthday to The Little Mermaid! Here are a few facts you didn't know|date=November 18, 2015|website=Deadite Den|access-date=April 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508133235/https://deaditeden.com/2015/11/18/happy-26th-birthday-to-the-little-mermaid-here-are-a-few-facts-you-didnt-know/|archive-date=May 8, 2016|url-status=dead}} this modification actually makes the character more similar to a [[squid]] than an octopus; whether or not Ursula is an octopus continues to be debated among both critics and fans, some of whom believe that the character's pair of arms actually account for the remaining two tentacles.{{Cite web|url=http://www.people.com/article/the-little-mermaid-25th-anniversary|title=Celebrate 25 Years of The Little Mermaid with 25 Things Even Superfans May Not Know|last=Mackie|first=Drew|date=November 14, 2014|website=People|publisher=Time Inc|access-date=April 22, 2016}} Clements admitted that the character's six tentacles made animating her a challenge nonetheless.{{Cite web|url=http://jetsettingmom.com/creating-disney-classic-interview-jon-musker-ron-clements-writers-directors-little-mermaid/|title=Creating a Disney Classic – Interview with John Musker & Ron Clements, writers & directors of The Little Mermaid!|date=September 11, 2013|website=Jet-Setting Mom|publisher=JETSETTING MOM|access-date=April 25, 2016}} Ursula was intentionally designed to instill fear in ''The Little Mermaid'''s viewers.{{Cite web|url=http://www.techtimes.com/articles/20379/20141117/the-little-mermaid-ursula-disney-villains.htm|title=Why Ursula From 'The Little Mermaid' is the Scariest Disney Villain|last=Rosenfeld|first=Laura|date=November 17, 2014|website=Tech Times|publisher=TechTimes Inc|access-date=May 26, 2016}} Animators studied [[The Terrible Dogfish|Monstro]] from Disney's ''[[Pinocchio (1940 film)|Pinocchio]]'' (1940) in order to animate the character's enlarged self emerging from the sea. Ursula's appearance was also based on that of the character [[Sunset Boulevard (film)|Norma Desmond]], who appears in the film ''[[Sunset Boulevard (film)|Sunset Boulevard]]'' (1950).{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wx8JsmNxjcUC&q=ursula+norma+desmond&pg=PA286|title=Film Theory Goes to the Movies: Cultural Analysis of Contemporary Film|last1=Collins|first1=Jim|last2=Collins|first2=Ava Preacher|last3=Radner|first3=Hilary|publisher=Routledge|year=2012|isbn=9781135216450|location=United Kingdom|pages=286}} Divine never lived to see his own likeness appear in ''The Little Mermaid''; the actor died in 1988, one year before the film's release. However, his cohorts agree that Divine would have greatly enjoyed Ursula. Documentarian [[Jeffrey Schwarz|Jeffrey Schwartz]] joked that the actor would have wanted to play Ursula himself had he known about the character, having once told Waters "When I was young, all I wanted to be was a Disney villain". ==Characterization and themes== [[About.com]]'s David Nusair observed that "There's no limit to how low Ursula will stoop to achieve her goals";{{Cite web|url=http://movies.about.com/od/animatedmovies/tp/disney-villains.htm|title=Top 10 Disney Villains|last=Nusair|first=David|website=About.com|access-date=April 23, 2016|archive-date=August 21, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821082614/http://movies.about.com/od/animatedmovies/tp/disney-villains.htm|url-status=dead}} the character often relies on a combination of [[Witchcraft|sorcery]] and deception to achieve them.{{Cite web|url=http://www.tvovermind.com/movies/ranking-top-10-animated-disney-villains|title=Ranking the Top 10 Animated Disney Villains|date=March 30, 2016|website=TVOvermind|access-date=April 25, 2016}} "A bargainer of the worst kind",{{Cite web|url=http://moviepilot.com/posts/1464097|title=Top Ten: Disney Animated Villains!|last=Eguizabal|first=William|date=June 1, 2014|website=Moviepilot|access-date=May 10, 2016|archive-date=June 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605035924/http://moviepilot.com/posts/1464097|url-status=dead}} Ursula only agrees to help the less fortunate when she's confident that she can gain something from them in return.{{citation needed|date=September 2024}} Identifying Ursula as Ariel's binary due to the character's experience and authority, ''Collision of Realities: Establishing Research on the Fantastic in Europe'' author Lars Schmeink described Ursula as a "more complex and mature character" than Ariel, embodying everything that the mermaid can potentially become.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t1znBQAAQBAJ&q=ursula+the+little+mermaid+feminist&pg=PA140|title=Collision of Realities: Establishing Research on the Fantastic in Europe|last1=Schmeink|first1=Lars|last2=Böger|first2=Astrid|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|year=2012|isbn=9783110276718|location=Germany|pages=140}} To Ariel, Ursula represents "the matronly image" who "instigate[s] the young princess' epic journey" as she longs to achieve the witch's "[[Sage (philosophy)|sage]]-like knowledge and power". Ursula teaches Ariel about [[womanhood]], a theme ''From Mouse to Mermaid: The Politics of Film, Gender, and Culture'' author Elizabeth Belle noticed is absent in Anderson's story. According to Bell, "Ursula can retrieve Ariel from her destined alliance with patriarchy", observing that the witch actually "teaches Ariel that performance and voice and manifestations" are "liberations of gender". ''[[Teen Ink]]'''s Emma James believes that Ursula's death ultimately prevents Ariel from experiencing and learning from the consequences of her actions, concluding, "Ariel never really owns up to all the mishap she caused." Observing that Ursula actually warns Ariel about the consequences should she fail to earn a kiss from Eric, Laura Stampler of ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' described the character as a "savvy contract negotiator".{{Cite magazine|url=https://time.com/3586569/sexist-little-mermaid/|title=The Little Mermaid: Not as Sexist as You Thought It Was|last1=Stampler|first1=Laura|last2=Dockterman|first2=Eliana|date=November 17, 2014|magazine=Time|publisher=Time Inc|access-date=April 22, 2016}} Writing for [[Collider (website)|Collider]], Dave Trumbore identified Ursula as the film's "Crossroads Demon".{{Cite web|url=https://collider.com/best-disney-villains/#ursula|title=Disney's 9 Most Wicked Animated Villains|last=Foutch|first=Haleigh|date=April 24, 2016|website=Collider.com|publisher=COMPLEX MEDIA INC|access-date=May 10, 2016}} According to Gary Thompson of the ''[[Philadelphia Daily News]]'', Ursula is similar to businesswoman [[Leona Helmsley]].{{Cite web|url=http://articles.philly.com/1989-11-17/entertainment/26137106_1_young-mermaid-evil-sea-witch-samuel-e-wright|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150409081112/http://articles.philly.com/1989-11-17/entertainment/26137106_1_young-mermaid-evil-sea-witch-samuel-e-wright|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 9, 2015|title=Back To The Drawing Boards Disney Regains Form With 'Mermaid' Tale|last=Thompson|first=Gary|date=November 17, 1989|website=Philly.com|access-date=April 6, 2016}} ''Makin' Toons: Inside the Most Popular Animated TV Shows and Movies'' author Allan Neuwirth observed that Ursula obeys Disney's "long-standing tradition of depicting classic scoundrels ... none so unsettling as their female villains." Neuwirth believes that the public's fear of Disney's female villains "stems from our expectations of nurturing, comfort and honesty from our mothers", while Disney's villainnesses, including Ursula, tend to "lust after ... youth and beauty."{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dFR9aLIA3g8C&q=ursula+matriarchy+disney&pg=PA34|title=Mommy Angst: Motherhood in American Popular Culture: Motherhood in American Popular Culture|last=Bishop|first=Mardia J.|publisher=ABC-CLIO|year=2009|isbn=9780313375316|location=United States|pages=33}} Ursula even goes as far as transforming herself into a beautiful young woman in order to trick Ariel's love interest into marrying her instead.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7Q5UVgMLxWcC&q=ursula+feminism+the+little+mermaid&pg=PA67|title=Bloody Mary in the Mirror: Essays in Psychoanalytic Folkloristics|last=Dundes|first=Alan|publisher=Univ. Press of Mississippi|year=2008|isbn=9781604731873|location=United States|pages=55–75}} Janet Wasko believes that Ursula's role as a powerful but antagonistic woman in ''The Little Mermaid'' alludes to the idea of [[patriarchy]] being preferable to [[matriarchy]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GQfk_5oMrCcC&q=ursula+matriarchy+disney&pg=PT128|title=Understanding Disney: The Manufacture of Fantasy|last=Wasko|first=Janet|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2013|isbn=9780745669045|location=United States}} Sophie Hall of [[Beamly]] identified Ursula as a woman struggling to "run the kingdom in a man's world, having been kicked out for no specific reason."{{Cite web|url=https://www.beamly.com/tv-film/8-disney-villains-better-heroes|title=8 Disney villains who are better than the heroes|last=Hall|first=Sophie|date=July 9, 2015|website=Beamly|access-date=April 25, 2016|archive-date=May 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508141935/https://www.beamly.com/tv-film/8-disney-villains-better-heroes|url-status=dead}} In her book ''Emerson Goes to the Movies: Individualism in Walt Disney Company's Post-1989 Animated Films'', author Justyna Fruzińska claimed that "the masculine rule of Triton is presented as positive and opposed to the negative, feminine rule of Ursula". ''Understanding Disney: The Manufacture of Fantasy'' author Janet Wasko accused the film's treatment of Ursula of "eliminat[ing] many of the female characters and undermin[ing] [the] feminine power" present in Andersen's fairy tale. However, Wasko also argued that Ursula could possibly be considered a [[mother figure]] for Ariel; the tunnel of Ursula's cave resembles a [[vagina]], while Ursula's mannerisms evoke those of a mother as she refers to Ariel as "my dear sweet child".{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lvKUm7D2vckC&q=ursula+feminism+the+little+mermaid&pg=PA158|title=Shakespeare Survey: Volume 56, Shakespeare and Comedy: An Annual Survey of Shakespeare Studies and Production|last=Holland|first=Peter|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2003|isbn=9780521827270|location=England|pages=158}} Gwynne Watkins of [[Yahoo!]] accused Ursula of "assur[ing] Ariel that human men prefer their women to be silent".{{Cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/movies/its-time-to-see-the-little-mermaid-as-a-feminist-102969568407.html|title=It's Time to See 'The Little Mermaid' as a Feminist Film|last=Watkins|first=Gwynne|date=November 18, 2014|website=Yahoo!|access-date=April 23, 2014}} Meanwhile, in response to feminist critiques of the character, author Amy M. Davis observed in her book ''Handsome Heroes and Vile Villains: Masculinity in Disney's Feature Films'' that Ursula is actually responsible for giving Eric the "power to make Ariel permanently human".{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0OQoCAAAQBAJ&q=ursula+the+little+mermaid+feminist&pg=PA169|title=Handsome Heroes and Vile Villains: Masculinity in Disney's Feature Films|last=Davis|first=Amy M|publisher=Indiana University Press|year=2014|isbn=9780861969074|pages=170}} However, author Alan Dundes in his book ''Bloody Mary in the Mirror: Essays in Psychoanalytic Folkloristics'' in conjunction with co-author Lauren Dundes observed that Ursula becomes masculine and deep-voiced once she acquires Triton's trident, implying that even "the only powerful woman in the story fulfills her desire for supreme power by becoming masculine". Dundes and Dundes also observed that Ursula reverts to being feminine once she is impaled. In her book ''Tales, Then and Now: More Folktales as Literary Fictions for Young Adults'', author Anna E. Altmann compared Ursula to [[Satan]] because both Ariel and Triton "sign a contract ... with her";{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TK0fOeuFiA0C&q=ursula+the+little+mermaid+feminist&pg=PA194|title=Tales, Then and Now: More Folktales as Literary Fictions for Young Adults|last=Altmann|first=Anna E|publisher=Libraries Unlimited|year=2001|isbn=9781563088315|location=United States|pages=194}} James Plath of Movie Metropolis described Ursula's contract as "a [[Deal with the Devil|Mephistophelean bargain]]."{{Cite web|url=http://moviemet.com/review/little-mermaid-3d-blu-ray-review |title=THE LITTLE MERMAID - 3D Blu-ray review |last=Plath |first=James |date=September 28, 2013 |website=Movie Metropolis |access-date=April 25, 2016 |quote=Ursula—one of the stronger Disney villains in the past several decades—gets her to sign on the dotted line of a Mephistophelean bargain. |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140208010138/http://moviemet.com/review/little-mermaid-3d-blu-ray-review |archive-date=February 8, 2014 }} Much like Satan, Ursula was banished from Triton's palace, similar to the way in which [[Lucifer]] was exiled from heaven. Felix Vasquez of Cinema Crazed believes that Ursula "is evil just for the sake of being evil".{{Cite web|url=http://cinema-crazed.com/blog/2013/09/30/the-little-mermaid-1989/|title=The Little Mermaid (1989)|last=Vasquez|first=Felix|date=September 30, 2013|website=Cinema Crazed|access-date=April 18, 2016}} Writing for the [[Disney.com|Disney Archives]], Dave Smith observed that Ursula "has the gross unsubtlety of Ratigan from '[[The Great Mouse Detective]]' but substantially more brio."{{Cite web|url=http://disney.go.com/vault/archives/villains/ursula/ursula.html |title=Ursula |last=Smith |first=Dave |website=Disney Archives |publisher=Disney |access-date=April 19, 2016 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100331195110/http://disney.go.com/vault/archives/villains/ursula/ursula.html |archive-date=March 31, 2010 }} Describing Ursula as "Bejeweled and lip-pouting like an overweight, over-rich, over-pampered, over-the-top society hostess gone mad," Smith perceived the character as "all flair, flamboyance, and theatricality mixed with a touch of con-artistry", citing [[Anger|wrath]] as her only genuine emotion. Additionally, Ursula tends to act as though she is performing for an audience. Jay Boyar of the ''[[Orlando Sentinel]]'' compared the character's appearance to that of evangelist [[Tammy Faye Messner|Tammy Faye]]. At times, Ursula tends to demonstrate stereotypically masculine physical traits.{{Cite web|url=http://www.threemoviebuffs.com/review/little-mermaid|title=The Little Mermaid|date=January 21, 2015|website=Three Movie Buffs|access-date=April 25, 2016}} Describing the character as "A campy sea witch with an insatiable thirst for power", ''[[Rolling Stone]]'''s David Ehrlich believes that Ursula resembles a child of Divine and [[Donald Trump]].{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/lists/12-scariest-moments-in-kids-films-20151019/the-little-mermaid-1989-ursula-supersized-20151019|title=12 Scariest Moments in Kids' Films|last=Ehrlich|first=David|date=October 19, 2015|magazine=Rolling Stone|access-date=April 25, 2016}} ==Appearances== ===Films=== ==== ''The Little Mermaid'' (1989) ==== Ursula debuted in the 1989 animated film ''[[The Little Mermaid (1989 film)|The Little Mermaid]]'' (where she is voiced by [[Pat Carroll]]), as a sea witch who is scheming to take advantage of the ambitions of Princess Ariel in order to get revenge on King Triton, usurp the throne and turning merpeople into [[polyps]] for her garden. When Ariel saves and falls in love with a human prince named Eric much to her father's chagrin, Ursula temporarily grants Ariel's wish to live as a human for three days in return for her voice. If she successfully earns a [[True love's kiss|kiss]] from Eric by the end of the third day, Ariel will remain human permanently; if she fails, she will turn back into a mermaid and belong to Ursula forever. However, Ursula is determined to sabotage Ariel's and Eric's budding romance at any cost; when she realizes that Ariel and Eric are actually falling in love, Ursula transforms herself into a beautiful young woman named "Vanessa" and hypnotizes Eric, tricking him into agreeing to marry her instead. Ariel manages to thwart Ursula and Eric's wedding. Eric realizes that it was Ariel who saved him when her voice returns to her and is about to kiss her, but as the sun sets Ariel transforms back into a mermaid and is captured by Ursula. Triton confronts Ursula and agrees to give up himself and his magical [[trident]] in return for Ariel's freedom. Ursula then uses the trident to expand into monstrous proportions and attempts to kill Ariel and Eric, but Eric manages to impale Ursula with the splintered bowsprit of a wrecked ship, and she dies. With Ursula gone, her powers cease, the merpeople turn back to normal, Triton's power is restored, and Ariel marries Eric once she is permanently transformed into a human. ====''The Little Mermaid 2: Return to the Sea''==== {{Main|The Little Mermaid 2: Return to the Sea}} Due to her death in the original film, Ursula does not appear in the direct-to-video sequel ''[[The Little Mermaid II: Return to the Sea]]'', but she is mentioned many times, mostly by her younger sister [[Morgana (The Little Mermaid)|Morgana]] (also voiced by Pat Carroll). Her image does appear in a photograph that Morgana has of Ursula. In the family portrait during the cut song "Gonna Get My Wish", Ursula was also depicted as a young girl with light green skin similar to Morgana and their mother. ====''Descendants 2''==== Ursula makes an appearance in the 2017 television film ''[[Descendants 2]]'', voiced by [[Whoopi Goldberg]]. Twenty years prior to the film, Ursula was banished on the Isle of the Lost with other villains. In the film, her daughter Uma (portrayed by [[China Anne McClain]]) is the main antagonist. During one scene, Ursula whips her tentacle out from the kitchen of her Fish and Chips shop and yells at Uma to stop singing and come to wash the dishes. While Ursula doesn't appear in other productions of the ''[[Descendants (franchise)|Descendants]]'' franchise, Uma returns in the sequel ''[[Descendants 3]]'', while in the spin-off film ''[[Descendants: The Rise of Red]]'' appears Ursula's younger sister Uliana (portrayed by [[Dara Reneé]]). ==== ''The Simpsons: Welcome to the Club''==== In ''[[The Simpsons Disney+ shorts|The Simpsons]]'' short ''[[Welcome to the Club (2022 film)|Welcome to the Club]]'', Ursula and other Disney villains welcome Lisa Simpson to "Disney Villain Land", and persuade her to become evil. She is voiced by [[Dawnn Lewis]].{{Cite web |last=Reif |first=Alex |date=2022-09-08 |title=TV Recap: "The Simpsons: Welcome to the Club" Brings Disney Villains to Springfield |url=https://www.laughingplace.com/w/articles/2022/09/08/tv-recap-the-simpsons-welcome-to-the-club-disney-plus/ |access-date=2022-09-09 |website=LaughingPlace.com }} ====''The Little Mermaid'' (2023)==== [[File:Little Mermaid Melissa McCarthy as Ursula (2023).jpg|thumb|215px|In Disney's 2023 live-action remake of ''The Little Mermaid'', Ursula was played by [[Melissa McCarthy]].]] Ursula appears in ''[[The Little Mermaid (2023 film)|The Little Mermaid]]'' (2023), portrayed by [[Melissa McCarthy]], while [[Jessica Alexander]] portrays her human form Vanessa. Similar to the broadway musical, this version is the estranged younger sister of King Triton and Ariel's aunt.{{Cite web|last1=Kroll|first1=Justin|date=2021-03-01|title=Jessica Alexander Joins Disney's Live-Action 'Little Mermaid' Pic|url=https://deadline.com/2021/03/jessica-alexander-disneys-little-mermaid-pic-1234704206/|access-date=2021-04-30|website=Deadline Hollywood|language=en-US}} ==== ''Once Upon a Studio'' ==== Ursula appears in ''[[Once Upon a Studio]]'' as part of the [[Walt Disney Animation Studios]] characters that appear gathering to take a group photo, voiced by archival recordings of Pat Carroll. ==== ''Lego Disney Princess: Villains Unite'' ==== Ursula appears as one of the antagonists in the [[Lego]] special for [[Disney+]] ''[[Lego Disney Princess: Villains Unite]]'' (2025).{{cite web |url=https://www.bsckids.com/2025/08/lego-disney-princess-villains-unite/ |title=LEGO Disney Princess: Villains Unite |author=Damon Cap |date=August 4, 2025 |website=BSCKids}} ===Television series=== ==== ''The Little Mermaid'' ==== Ursula appears as the antagonist in four episodes of ''[[The Little Mermaid (TV series)|The Little Mermaid]]'' prequel television series: "Against the Tide", "Tail of Two Crabs", "Heroes" and "Ariel's Treasures". In all four episodes, she executes various plans to antagonize King Triton and take over Atlantica, but all fail. ====''House of Mouse''==== Ursula makes recurring appearances in ''[[House of Mouse]]'' (2001) as a guest at the eponymous nightclub, with Pat Carroll reprising the role. In the film ''[[Mickey's House of Villains]]'', Ursula and [[Jafar (Aladdin)|Jafar]], among other villains, work together to take over the club.{{cite AV media|title=Mickey's House of Villains|date=2002|people=Jamie Mitchell|publisher=Walt Disney Television Animation|location=USA|medium=Television production}} ====''Once Upon a Time''==== Two live-action versions of Ursula appear in the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] television series ''[[Once Upon a Time (TV series)|Once Upon a Time]]''. ====="The Sea Goddess"===== Ursula the Sea Goddess appears in the [[Once Upon a Time season 3|third season]], voiced by [[Yvette Nicole Brown]]. In the episode "[[Ariel (Once Upon a Time)|Ariel]]", she is described as a sea goddess whom no one has seen for a thousand years. According to Ariel, Ursula gave merfolk the ability to gain legs once a year, when the tide is highest. Ariel uses this ability to visit Prince Eric at his castle, where he is having a ball honoring Ursula. Later, the [[Regina Mills|Evil Queen]] ([[Lana Parrilla]]) disguises herself as Ursula to make a deal with Ariel and trick her into capturing Snow White. ====="The Sea Witch"===== {{Infobox character | name = Ursula the Sea Witch | image = Ursula once upon a time.png | caption = Ursula the Sea Witch, in ''Once Upon a Time'' | first = "[[Heroes and Villains (Once Upon a Time)|Heroes and Villains]]" (Season 4; Episode 12) | creator = [[Edward Kitsis]] and [[Adam Horowitz]] | portrayer = {{Plainlist| *[[Merrin Dungey]] *[[Tiffany Boone]] (young) }} | species = [[Mermaid]] (original)
Human (via [[Shapeshifting|Magical transformation]]) | gender = Female | occupation = [[Magician (fantasy)|Sorceress]] | title = The Sea Witch
Queen of Darkness | affiliation = Queens of Darkness (formerly) | nationality = Atlantican | family = {{Plainlist| *[[Poseidon]] {{small|(father)}}{{cite web|title=Ernie Hudson To Play Poseidon On '''Once Upon a Time'''|url=https://deadline.com/2014/12/ernie-hudson-cast-poseidon-once-upon-a-time-abc-1201330792/|access-date=February 3, 2015|date=December 19, 2014|website=deadline.com|publisher=Deadline|last=Brooks|first=Larry|archive-date=December 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224164519/http://deadline.com/2014/12/ernie-hudson-cast-poseidon-once-upon-a-time-abc-1201330792/|url-status=dead}} *Unnamed mother {{small|(deceased)}} }} }} Ursula the Sea Witch appears as an antagonist of the second half of the [[Once Upon a Time (season 4)|fourth season]], where she is portrayed as an adult by [[Merrin Dungey]], and as a teenager by [[Tiffany Boone]]. The episode "[[Poor Unfortunate Soul]]" contains flashbacks to Ursula's youth, when she was a teenage [[mermaid]] living under the sea with her father King [[Poseidon]] ([[Ernie Hudson]]). Ursula was gifted with a beautiful voice, which Poseidon wanted her to use to lure pirates to their death, in order to avenge the murder of Ursula's mother at the hands of an unnamed pirate. Ursula refused and instead befriended a pirate, Captain Hook ([[Colin O'Donoghue]]), who supported her desire for freedom. Ursula and Hook's friendship fell apart when Hook sealed Ursula's singing voice inside an enchanted shell to punish Poseidon for destroying a weapon Hook wanted for himself. Ursula, angered and disappointed with both merfolk and humans, used Poseidon's trident to transform her tail into tentacles, emulating the ancient sea goddess that she was named after. The episodes "[[Heroes and Villains (Once Upon a Time)|Heroes and Villains]]" and "[[Darkness on the Edge of Town (Once Upon a Time)|Darkness on the Edge of Town]]" contain flashbacks to the Enchanted Forest of the past, where Ursula teamed up with fellow witches [[Maleficent#Once Upon a Time|Maleficent]] ([[Kristin Bauer van Straten]]) and [[Cruella de Vil#Once Upon a Time|Cruella De Vil]] ([[Victoria Smurfit]]). The three of them worked together to try to defeat the heroes and find their happy endings, but failed. In the episode "[[Best Laid Plans (Once Upon a Time)|Best Laid Plans]]", while trying to rescue Maleficent's baby from Snow and Charming, Ursula and Cruella fell into a portal that lead into the non-magical world. Three decades later, in modern-day New York, Ursula is working as a cleaner in an aquarium when she is recruited by Rumplestiltskin, who also reunites her with Cruella. Ursula, Cruella and Rumplestiltskin then trick their way into entering the magical town of Storybrooke. In the episode "[[Unforgiven (Once Upon a Time)|Unforgiven]]", they resurrect Maleficent to join their group. In the present-day plotline of "Poor Unfortunate Soul", a remorseful Hook makes a deal with Ursula to get her singing voice back. They are only successful when Ariel intercedes, bringing Poseidon to Storybrooke so that he and Ursula can reconcile, and the enchantment is broken. Having achieved her happy ending, Ursula tells Hook the full plan Rumplestiltskin has for the heroes, and afterward returns to the sea with her father. {{Clear}} ====''The Wonderful World of Mickey Mouse''==== Ursula appears in ''[[The Wonderful World of Mickey Mouse]]'' episode "Keep on Rollin'", with Pat Carroll reprising the role, where along with [[Pete (Disney)|Pete]] and the [[Beagle Boys]] confront [[Mickey Mouse]] and his friends for being in the skating rink where the characters meet.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/snyde/ny-disney-mickey-mouse-20201117-uqp5hegqrzey3i4q36ku7adhfe-story.html|title=EXCLUSIVE VIDEO: Special cameos from historic characters appear in new Mickey Mouse shorts at Disney+|website=[[New York Daily News]]|date=17 November 2020 }} ==== ''Ariel'' ==== Ursula appears in ''[[Ariel (TV series)|Ariel]]'', voiced by [[Amber Riley]]. Ursula makes an appearance in flashback when the game's protagonist dreams of the events of the first film in Book 3. ===Theme park attractions=== Ursula appears in Disney park attractions such as the ''[[Fantasmic!]]'' show debuted in 1992 at Disneyland Park, as one of the [[Disney Villains]] summoned to destroy [[Mickey Mouse]]. A massive Ursula [[Audio-Animatronics|Audio-Animatronic]] appears in [[The Little Mermaid ~ Ariel's Undersea Adventure]], a dark ride at [[Disney California Adventure]], and [[Magic Kingdom]]. Ursula is a central character in the annual [[Halloween]]-themed [[fireworks]] show [[HalloWishes]] at the [[Walt Disney World]] [[Magic Kingdom]] ''[[Mickey's Not-So-Scary Halloween Party]]'' "hard ticket" event. Ursula also appears at the tail end of the ''Little Mermaid'' unit in [[Walt Disney's Parade of Dreams]] at [[Disneyland]]. ===Stage=== ====Broadway musical==== {{main|The Little Mermaid (musical)}} In the [[The Little Mermaid (musical)|musical version]] of the original film, [[Sherie Rene Scott]] originated the live role, which she played until January 25, 2009. Other actresses who played the role include [[Heidi Blickenstaff]] and [[Faith Prince]].{{cite web |author=The Broadway League |date=January 10, 2008 |title=The Little Mermaid – Broadway Musical – Original |url=https://www.ibdb.com/broadway-production/the-little-mermaid-456222 |access-date=December 6, 2021 |website=IBDB |archive-date=January 18, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180118052201/https://www.ibdb.com/broadway-production/the-little-mermaid-456222 |url-status=live}}
{{cite web |title=The Little Mermaid Broadway @ Lunt-Fontanne Theatre |url=http://www.playbill.com/production/the-little-mermaid-lunt-fontanne-theatre-vault-0000005011 |access-date=December 6, 2021 |website=Playbill |archive-date=November 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125091310/https://www.playbill.com/production/the-little-mermaid-lunt-fontanne-theatre-vault-0000005011 |url-status=live}} In this version, Ursula is King Triton's sister, a concept for the original film that was eventually dropped.(2006) ''Treasures Untold: The Making of Disney's 'The Little Mermaid'' [Documentary featurette]. Bonus material from ''The Little Mermaid: Platinum Edition'' DVD. Walt Disney Home Entertainment. When Ursula and Triton's father died, the pair were given an equal share of the sea plus two magical items. Triton received the trident while Ursula received the magic Nautilus shell. Though the two were meant to rule the seas together, Ursula's greed and use of dark magic to usurp Triton led to her being banished. The desire for revenge and power is her motivation for the show. The musical's plot is similar to the film, with the exception that Ursula doesn't transform into Vanessa, and she is ultimately defeated by Ariel rather than Eric when the mermaid destroys the Nautilus shell that contains Ursula's power. In the revamped version of the musical developed by Glenn Casale in 2012, Ursula and Triton's backstory was changed, making her the youngest of seven sisters like Ariel. Unlike Ariel, she was not a beautiful mermaid like her sisters and was despised and ignored by their father [[Poseidon]] while her sisters were adored. She gained the Nautilus shell when Poseidon gave it to her to ease the guilt he felt for how he treated her. Using the shell, Ursula killed all of her sisters and became queen after Poseidon died from a “very rare and lethal flu”. She forgot he had Triton, then only one-year-old, and dismissed him as a threat until he became old enough to depose her and become king. Ursula's motivation for revenge otherwise remains similar to the original book of the musical, with the addition that she was the one who killed Ariel's mother. In addition to her song from the film, [[Alan Menken]] and [[Glenn Slater]] wrote new songs for Ursula: "I Want the Good Times Back", which introduces Ursula and her backstory, "I Want the Good Times Back (reprise)", where Ursula orders Flotsam and Jetsam to sabotage Ariel's attempt to get Eric to kiss her, and a reprise of "[[Poor Unfortunate Souls]]", where Ursula forces Triton to sign a deal and claims the trident. In the workshop stage, Ursula had a different introductory song: "Wasting Away" where she sings about her suffering in exile after Triton deposed her for using black magic, and its reprise featured Ursula preparing to transform into Vanessa.{{cite book|last=Lassell|first=Michael|title =The Little Mermaid: A Broadway Musical - From the Deep Blue Sea to the Great White Way|publisher =Disney Editions New York|year =2009|isbn =978-1-4231-1272-3}} [[Emily Skinner (actress, born 1970)|Emily Skinner]] provided vocals for Ursula in the workshop. In the 2012 revamped version of the musical, "I Want the Good Times Back" is replaced with a new song, "Daddy's Little Angel".{{cite web | last=Hill | first=Jim | title=How Glenn Casale Helped The Little Mermaid Find Her Feet After This Disney Stage Show Stumbled on Broadway | date=2014-07-23 | url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/jim-hill/how-glenn-casale-helped-t_b_5612802.html | publisher=Huffington Post | access-date=2016-08-05 }} ==== Unfortunate - The Untold Story of Ursula The Sea Witch (2019-present) ==== Ursula becomes the main character in a [[revisionism (fictional)|revisionist]] parody musical [[Unfortunate - The Untold Story of Ursula The Sea Witch]] by Robyn Grant.{{cite news |last1=Stone |first1=Mee-Lai |title=All dressed up with nowhere to play: Edinburgh's stranded fringe stars – in pictures |url=https://www.theguardian.com/stage/gallery/2020/aug/19/edinburgh-stranded-fringe-stars-in-pictures |work=the Guardian |date=19 August 2020}}{{cite news |last1=Wyver |first1=Kate |title=Unfortunate: The Untold Story of Ursula the Sea Witch review – a chaotic camp delight |url=https://www.theguardian.com/stage/2024/jan/12/unfortunate-the-untold-story-of-ursula-the-sea-witch-review-southwark-playhouse-elephant-london |work=The Guardian |date=12 January 2024}}{{cite news |last1=Ferris |first1=Nick |title=Unfortunate: The Untold Story of Ursula the Sea Witch: The Little Mermaid gets Wicked |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/theatre/what-to-see/unfortunate-the-untold-story-of-ursula-the-sea-witch-review/ |work=The Telegraph |date=10 January 2024}} ==== Other stage productions ==== In 2016, [[Rebel Wilson]] performed the role of Ursula at a stripped-down concert version of ''The Little Mermaid'' at the [[Hollywood Bowl]], which featured the songs from the film and four songs from the Broadway musical.{{cite web|last=Riley|first=Jenelle|date=2016-06-04|title=L.A. Theater Review: 'The Little Mermaid in Concert' at the Hollywood Bowl|url=https://variety.com/2016/legit/reviews/little-mermaid-in-concert-at-the-hollywood-bowl-1201788875/|access-date=2016-06-22|publisher=Variety.com}} Wilson was praised for her performance, which was described by ''The Huffington Post'' as "[[Pitch (music)|pitch]] perfect".{{cite web|last=Cuccinello|first=Hayley|date=2016-06-06|title=Rebel Wilson Is The Ursula We Always Wanted In 'The Little Mermaid Live'|website=[[HuffPost]]|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/rebel-wilson-is-the-ursula-we-always-wanted-in-the-little-mermaid-live_us_57556b31e4b0c3752dce06b9|access-date=2016-06-22}} [[Queen Latifah]] portrayed Ursula in the 2019 television special, ''[[The Little Mermaid Live!]]'' which used a similar format of the live concerts at the Hollywood Bowl, by combining a screening of the film with live accompaniment by guest musicians and celebrities.{{Cite web|last=Bentley|first=Jean|date=August 5, 2019|title=Little Mermaid' Live Starring Auli'i Cravalho Set at ABC|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/little-mermaid-live-starring-aulii-cravalho-set-at-abc-1229130|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016044739/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/little-mermaid-live-starring-aulii-cravalho-set-at-abc-1229130|archive-date=October 16, 2019|access-date=October 16, 2019|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}} ===Literature=== Ursula has appeared in various Disney Press novels and tie-ins for the franchise. A comic book series, ''Disney's The Little Mermaid'', was released in 1992, revolving around the adventures of Ariel living under the sea as a mermaid. Ursula appears in a few issues, notably "Serpent Teen", which depicts how Ursula obtained the sea serpent carcass that makes her home.{{cite comic|writer=Peter David|penciller=Bill Fugate|inker=Dave Hunt|title=Serpent Teen|volume=1|issue=1|date=1992|publisher=Walt Disney Magazine Publishing Group}} ''My Side of the Story: Ursula'' (2004) retells the plot of the film from Ursula's point of view, and depicts Ursula having romantic feelings for Triton.{{cite book|last=Skinner|first=Daphne|title=My Side of the Story: Ursula|publisher=Disney Press|date=2004|location=New York|isbn=0-7868-3503-6|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/mysideofstory00skin}} ''The Villain Files'' (2005) depicts Ursula's youth living in Triton's castle while Ariel was a baby.{{cite book|last=Pringle|first=Betsy Henry|title=Disney Villains: The Top Secret Files|publisher=Disney Press|date=2005|location=New York|isbn=0-7868-3603-2}} Ursula is a main character in the 2016 [[young adult fiction|young adult]] novel ''Poor Unfortunate Soul: A Tale of the Sea Witch'' by [[Serena Valentino]].{{cite book | title=Poor Unfortunate Soul: A Tale of the Sea Witch | isbn=978-1484724057 | last1=Valentino | first1=Serena | date=26 July 2016 | publisher=Disney Press }}{{cite web | title=Serena Valentino (official website): Poor Unfortunate Soul | url=http://www.serenavalentino.com/projects/ursula/ | access-date=2016-04-10 | archive-date=2016-04-13 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160413140705/http://www.serenavalentino.com/projects/ursula/ | url-status=dead }} The novel is the third entry of the "Villains" series, a [[shared universe]] that [[Crossover (fiction)|crosses over]] various theatrical Disney films including ''[[Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)|Beauty and the Beast]]'', ''[[Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937 film)|Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs]]'' and ''[[Sleeping Beauty (1959 film)|Sleeping Beauty]]''. In this novel, Ursula is King Triton's younger sister who was betrayed by him as a child for choosing a tentacled form instead of a mermaid's tail, and grew up as a human in the town of Ipswich with an adoptive human father. Ursula returned to the sea when her adopted father was killed by the townsfolk for protecting her, befriending Athena, Queen of Atlantica, but was denied her inheritance by Triton and banished to the shadows. Ursula conspires with three other witches to steal Triton's soul and become ruler of all the seas, but is ultimately defeated.{{cite book | first=Serena | last=Valentino | date=2016 | title=Poor Unfortunate Soul | publisher=Disney Press | isbn=9781484724057 }} Ursula is the villain in the 2020 children's horror novel ''Part of Your Nightmare'' by Vera Strange, which is the first book of the ''Disney Chills'' series.{{ cite book | first=Vera | last=Strange | title=Part of Your Nightmare | date=7 July 2020 | publisher=Disney Press | isbn=9781368048255 }} The novel's setting is modern day, in a beach city named Triton Bay where eleven-year-old Shelly Anderson has just moved to a new school. Shelly struggles to fit in and especially wants the approval of Kendall, the popular captain of their school's swim team. Shelly first encounters Ursula at the aquarium owned by the Anderson family, and afterward has sleeping and waking nightmares of Ursula offering her a deal where that Shelly can be the "fastest swimmer ever", if Shelly does her a small favor in return. ==== ''Poor Unfortunate Soul: A Tale of the Sea Witch'' ==== Ursula is mentioned and appears in the second book of the Villains series by [[Serena Valentino]], ''The Beast Within: A Tale of Beauty's Prince'', appearing before the Odd Sisters. She is the main character in the third book. Prior to the events of the book, Ursula appears in the English town of [[Ipswich]] and proceeds to inflict pain on the citizens of the town and turn them into twisted sea creatures before being stopped by [[King Triton]]. Years later, Ursula, in her guise as Vanessa, goes to the Odd Sisters and asks for their help to defeat Triton, who in the book is Ursula's brother and therefore makes Ursula Ariel's aunt, in exchange for helping them find their sister, Circe. Unknown to the Odd Sisters, Ursula has turned Circe into one of her polyps and is keeping her captive in her cavern. Initially the Odd Sisters help her, but upon discovering that Ursula is keeping Circe captive, they turn on her and use their magic to influence Eric's ship to impale Ursula and kill her as revenge for keeping Circe captive. Circe is freed after this and discovers Ursula's golden shell. After finding out that her sisters killed Ursula, she banishes them to sleep to keep them from harming anyone else. In the fourth book ''Mistress of All Evil: A Tale of the Dark Fairy'', Circe and Nanny gather Ursula's remains and give her a burial at sea prior to Maleficent's arrival. ==== ''Part of Your World: A Twisted Tale'' ==== The fifth book in the ''[[A Twisted Tale]]'' series written by author Liz Braswell, it addresses the question "''What if Ariel had never defeated Ursula?''" In the book Ursula, in her guise as Vanessa, ultimately wed Prince Eric and still possesses Ariel's voice five years later, and uses Eric's connections to go to war with neighboring kingdoms and expand the territory of Eric's kingdom. She maintains a beautiful appearance and a rich lifestyle. She is ultimately overthrown, by Ariel and Eric. In this book Braswell describes Ursula's species as “cecaelia,”{{Cite book |last=Braswell |first=Liz |title=Part of Your World (A Twisted Tale) |publisher=Disney-Hyperion |year=2018 |pages=122}} a term created by fans in the late 2000s.{{Cite book |last=Hayward |first=Philip |url={{GBurl|id=MSkBDgAAQBAJ|q=Cecaelia|p=37}} |title=Making a Splash |year=2017 |pages=37|publisher=Indiana University Press |isbn=978-0-86196-925-8}} This was the first Disney-published work to use the name. ==== ''Part of Your Nightmare'' ==== Ursula is the primary antagonist in the first book of the ''Disney Chills'' book series titled ''Part of Your Nightmare'', written by author Jennifer Brody under the name of Vera Strange. The book was published on July 7, 2020. In the book, Ursula agrees to make protagonist Shelley more popular at her school. However, Shelley soon discovers that this deal comes with a price, one she may not be willing to pay. ==== ''Vanessa - Happily Never After'' ==== Ursula, in her guise as Vanessa, is the main character in a novel titled ''Vanessa - Happily Never After'', written in [[French language|French]] by Lorie Langdon. The book was published on January 12, 2022. Disappointed by the sea people who reject her, Ursula, now Vanessa, ventures to land for the first time, where she sets out in search of the ultimate power which will make her so powerful that no one will ever be able to ignore her again. But destiny leads her to André Baros, a simple human with whom she falls in love... Can she really have it all? Love and power?
